name: Leo Africanus
summary: A Granada-born Fez diplomat travels to Timbuktu and the eastern Mediterranean, is captured by Christian corsairs, baptised by Pope Leo X, and writes in Italy the Description of Africa.

stops.note: Born al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Wazzan shortly after the city's fall to Castile.
His family settles in Fez, where he studies at the Qarawiyyin.
Crosses the Atlas with his uncle's embassy to the Songhay.
Describes the city's scholars, judges and book trade under Askia Muhammad.
Describes the Songhay royal city and its market.
Serves the Wattasid sultan Muhammad al-Burtughali on missions in Morocco.
Carries a mission from the sultan of Fez to the Ottoman court.
Is in the port during the Ottoman conquest of Mamluk Egypt.
Sees the city just after Selim I's conquest.
Travels up the Nile before crossing to the Red Sea.
Captured at sea by Spanish corsairs and held by the Knights Hospitaller.
Presented to Leo X, imprisoned in Castel Sant'Angelo, then baptised in St Peter's in 1520.
Writes an Arabic-Hebrew-Latin medical vocabulary for Jacob Mantino.
Finishes his manuscript on African geography under Clement VII.
Probably leaves Italy before the Sack of Rome and returns to Islam in Tunis.

sources.cite: Natalie Zemon Davis, Trickster Travels: A Sixteenth-Century Muslim Between Worlds, New York 2006
Leo Africanus, Description of Africa, ed. G. B. Ramusio, Venice 1550
